abstract: This chapter contends that mechanization in 18th-century Britain depended less on heroic individual invention than on a combination of three conditions: cheap coal, expensive labor, and an unusually open patent regime. The author maintains that without this coalition, the same engineering ideas would likely have stayed curiosities rather than becoming widespread industrial practice. The introduction states the thesis and previews that subsequent sections will examine each factor in turn. The excerpt provided is only the opening framing and does not include the evidence for each factor.
